items.title: The Gysin class at infinity commutes with every bivariant class pulled back from a locally finite type morphism
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Extending the Gysin-at-infinity lemma, the statement says that for a morphism f : Y -> X locally of finite type and a class c in A^*(Y -> X), the class C of that lemma satisfies C o c = c o C in A^*(W_infinity x_X Y -> X) (statement lines 10155-10160). The proof builds the full cartesian diagram of W_Y over W over P^1_Y over Y and W_Y over P^1_X over X, picks beta in CH_{k+1}(W) restricting to the flat pullback of alpha on b^{-1}(A^1_X), observes that c cap beta restricts to the flat pullback of c cap alpha on b_Y^{-1}(A^1_Y), and then compares i_{Y,infinity}^*(c cap beta) with c cap i_infinity^* beta using that c is a bivariant class; this is exactly the identity C cap c cap alpha = c cap C cap alpha, and the same argument repeats after any base change by X' -> X locally of finite type (proof lines 10163-10188). Matching the two compatibilities, one for the class c and one for the defining property of C, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
